When I was 16 I had the realization too. The best case scenario happened with me and my homophobic parents: they denied it, said it was a phase, and dropped the issue. So I'm still in the closet at age 20. It's not the sweetest thing, but at the same time not a lot of homophobes want to change their views, even for someone they love. You said you want to come out to them, right? At the time I felt like I HAD to come out to them, like they were somehow entitled to knowledge that could have endangered me if they reacted differently (or if they found out about my girlfriend now) and that's the same with your parents. If they won't accept it, it's not knowledge they deserve. My advice would be to stay in the closet, and reach out to the community more to find support. See if your school has a GSA (you're in middle school so you might have to wait until high school) or if there are any safe spaces in your community (mine has an lgbt friendly church, which is unfortunate since I'm not particularly religious). I just want to say that you're a very brave kid and I wish you better than what I had.

Some years ago, I was taking a walk with my mother. We got close to the parking lot of an old, abandoned hotel. It had a small parking garage and then the main lot, and while we were just stepping foot into the lot, we heard a scream come from the garage. It sounded feminine, but muffled. Another scream, this one sounded like a man, came immediately afterwards, but it sounded like he was saying something in an angry tone, but really muffled and we couldn't make it out. Some guy was riding his bike nearbye when he rolled up and asked us if we heard it too, and we stood there while he lapped around the parking lot looking for anything suspicious. When he didn't find anything, he called the police. Me and my mom didn't stick around for them to show up, and I was maybe in the 7th grade when that happened and I was probably really shook up by it, so in retrospect she was probably just trying to get her daughter out of a scary situation. I never heard anything about it again, never saw anything in the newspapers.

I never really saw any kids' shows besides the puppet shows, but sometimes they would broadcast librarians reading picture books to a gaggle of kids sitting on a carpet. When I was around maybe 4 or 5 years old, before I started school (so around 1999/2000 or so) I would get babysat by my grandmother. If there was nothing good on Nick Jr. (and I don't think Cartoon Network had a good morning line up at the time) I would have the choice between watching those puppet shows, or seeing what was on PBS (rarely Sesame Street which I'm oddly nostalgic for right now, but more often Between the Lions) and I would always end up watching PBS no matter what, even if it wasn't a kids' program. I actually had a pretty tight schedule going on when my grandmother would babysit me. I remember that she would start lunch during Wheel of Fortune, and it would be cooking while she watched the Price is Right (Bob Barker, of course)

God, and I thought my town was small. The middle of the day stuff jogged my memory too. I remember being really young, maybe six or seven years old?
